dimensions.title: Cognitive
milestones: Can solve simple addition and subtraction problems
activities: Play board games that involve counting
Engage in simple puzzles
Ask questions that require problem-solving

dimensions.title: Language
milestones: Uses complex sentences with multiple clauses
Has a vocabulary of around 2000 words
activities: Read age-appropriate books together
Encourage storytelling by prompting with questions
Play rhyming or word games
watchFor: Struggles with understanding or following conversations

dimensions.title: Physical
milestones: Can skip, hop on one foot, and jump with coordination
activities: Encourage outdoor play with ball games
Provide art supplies for cutting and pasting
Engage in obstacle courses
watchFor: Difficulty with tasks requiring fine motor skills

dimensions.title: Social
milestones: Can cooperate and negotiate with peers
activities: Arrange playdates with peers
Encourage team sports or group activities
Discuss emotions and empathy through storytelling
watchFor: Struggles to make or maintain friendships
Displays aggressive or overly passive behaviors in groups

dimensions.title: Emotional
milestones: Can express a wider range of emotions
Begins to use strategies to manage frustration
activities: Teach calming techniques like deep breathing
Discuss feelings and how to handle them
Role-play different emotional scenarios
watchFor: A lack of interest in activities they previously enjoyed

dimensions.title: Curiosity
milestones: Asks many questions about the world
Shows interest in how things work
activities: Visit science museums or nature centers
Engage in simple experiments like growing plants
Encourage a scavenger hunt

dimensions.title: Learning
milestones: Can focus for longer periods on activities
Starts to develop preference for learning styles
activities: Set dedicated time for homework or reading
Use learning apps or games
Encourage project-based learning like building models
watchFor: Gives up quickly on challenging tasks
Lacks motivation to engage in learning activities

dimensions.title: Independence
activities: Assign small household tasks
Encourage them to make decisions about activities or meals
Teach them to manage their belongings
watchFor: Reliance on adults for basic tasks
Shows resistance to trying new things independently
